tasks.short: Meet parents and guardians to discuss progress and agree priorities and resource needs.

steps.what: Read children's marks on the pupil record
Draft a progress note from those children's marks

loop.input: The mark extract and the class teacher's own short notes.
loop.output: A progress note for this meeting.
loop.check: Each sentence cites a mark or a stored note and adds no diagnostic label and no emotion guess.
loop.stop: The class teacher accepts this version or rewrites it after two drafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed comment bank cannot tell whether a sentence matches this child's marks.

steps.what: Meet parents and guardians to discuss children's progress
Determine priorities and resource needs with the parents
Mail the agreed priorities to parents and guardians
File the agreed priorities on the pupil record

tasks.design: A scheduled read on the {OTHER} pupil record fills a {DOCS} progress note from stored marks, and the class teacher accepts or rewrites it before the meeting. The meeting stays in the room. Afterwards the teacher sends the {EMAIL} message they wrote and files the priority and resource codes on the {OTHER} record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Marks sat in the pupil record, but the note and the meeting were free conversation, so a template could not say what was true for this child.
tasks.enabler_now: A short draft can be checked sentence by sentence against stored marks, and the teacher still holds the meeting.
tasks.still_hard: Parents bring news the record does not have, and a wrong note can harm the relationship. The conversation does not compress.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher hears what the parents want and agrees priorities in the room. A draft cannot do that.
tasks.altitude: The parent meeting still takes the hour. The teacher no longer hunts marks beforehand and still decides the priorities in the room.

reach.task: Read the filed priorities before a support conversation
reach.learn: which priority and resource codes the class teacher already agreed with the parents

evidence.claim: ParnasSys holds pupil records and learning-goal tracking, so a progress note is a query of marks already stored. It does not run the parent meeting.
WOR does not apply to schools. Under the WMS, parents and pupils have a say in pupil-data rules, and staff consent applies to tools that can monitor staff.
Inferring pupils' emotions is banned, so the progress note must not guess how a child feels.
A pupil progress sheet is a query of stored marks plus a short note. The parent meeting itself stays a conversation.

assumptions: The focal boundary is the class teacher's own prep, the meeting, the mail and the filing. Parents' speaking time sits inside that meeting and is not a separate baseline.

The {OTHER} pupil record already stores pupil id, subject code, mark, mark date and attendance count, produced by the class teacher or the school office. If a mark is only on paper, the teacher types it before the extract runs.
Priority and resource codes are a short school list: extra reading, language support, materials, or none. A need that is not on the list stays as the teacher's own sentence in the mail.
The 1.5 incremental hours are rejected-draft rework and code upkeep beyond the review already in the draft step. Test the native pupil-record view before any custom screen.
unknowns: Whether this school stores marks in the pupil record or only in a paper mark book.
Whether parents expect a written note after every meeting.
research_questions: What share of parent meetings currently has a written progress note?

already_counted.description: The meeting and the priority decision stay with the class teacher.
The teacher still edits the progress note, writes anything sensitive in the mail, and picks the priority and resource codes.

incremental.description: Each term, correct progress-note drafts the trace check rejected and keep the priority and resource codes current.

approvals.approved_version: parent message version the class teacher sends after the meeting

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The parent meeting and the priority decision stay. Many meetings have little written prep, so the low end is a short note or none. The high end is only the mark extract, half the note draft, and part of the mail and the filing. The meeting hour is not claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Use computers, audio-visual aids and other materials during presentations.

steps.what: Choose the point these materials should supplement
Make materials that supplement the presentations

loop.input: The named supplement point and the year-group level.
loop.output: A supplement file for this lesson.
loop.check: The aid matches the lesson point and the year-group reading level and names no pupil.
loop.stop: The class teacher accepts this version or rewrites it after two drafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: A stored clip library cannot tell which material fits this lesson's point.

steps.what: Set up the computers and the audio-visual equipment
Use that equipment while giving the presentations

tasks.design: The class teacher names the point to supplement. A draft on {DOCS} proposes the materials from that point and the year-group level, and the teacher accepts the version before the lesson. Setting up the computers and giving the presentation stay in the room.
tasks.previous_blocker: Choosing what will help this class, and running the equipment while teaching, is situational. A clip library does not know today's point.
tasks.enabler_now: Drafting a worksheet or a short sequence from a named lesson point is now a bounded check: it matches the point, the level, and it names no pupil.
tasks.still_hard: The live presentation and the equipment setup stay. A good aid still fails if the class does not follow.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher sees the room and changes what they show. The draft only proposes the materials.

ambition.what: which single point the presentation supplements, before new materials are made.

tasks.altitude: The presentation still happens in the room. The teacher decides which point to supplement before new materials are made, and still accepts the aid.

reach.task: Open the accepted supplement file for a small group
reach.learn: which point the class teacher chose to supplement and which file was accepted

evidence.claim: Snappet drafts a class activity for the lesson goal. The teacher still gives the presentation.
LessonUp rewrites lesson text at another level, summarises it and translates it. That can reshape a worksheet. The teacher still gives the presentation.

Oak's Aila, in a randomised trial of 464 primary teachers in 108 English schools, cut weekly preparation from 3.3 to 2.5 hours and quality was no worse. It covered 7% of lessons, use declined over ten weeks, and under one in five teachers felt it meaningfully influenced their teaching. That measures material-prep time, not the presentation hour.

assumptions: The focal boundary is the class teacher choosing, making and using the aid in their own presentation. Students have no labour share.
A lesson objective or topic line already exists in {DOCS} before the aid is drafted. If it does not, the teacher types one line and the draft waits.
The materials name no pupil and hold public lesson content only. Lesson file fields are lesson id, objective code, year group and aid file.
The 1.2 incremental hours cover retiring aids when the goal list changes. The per-aid review is already in the make step. Test native lesson-file fields before any custom screen.
unknowns: Whether classrooms have a fixed computer and display or a shared trolley.
How often materials are reused across years.
research_questions: What share of presentation time is making a new aid versus playing one that exists?

already_counted.description: Setting up the equipment and giving the presentation stay with the class teacher.
The teacher still chooses the point and still edits the aid before accepting it.

incremental.description: Retire aids that no longer match the goal list. The per-aid review is already in the make step.

approvals.approved_version: supplement file version the class teacher accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only making the aid changes. Setup and the live presentation stay. A primary trial covered 7 percent of lessons and use fell over ten weeks, so the high end is a minority of lessons. The presentation hour is not claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet other professionals to discuss one student's needs and progress.

steps.what: Read one individual student's marks and support notes
Draft the brief on that student's needs and progress

loop.input: Stored marks, the current support code and the class teacher's notes.
loop.output: A student brief for the invited professionals.
loop.check: Each sentence traces to a stored mark or note, names no diagnosis, infers no emotion, and the recipient list is only the invited professionals.
loop.stop: The class teacher accepts this version or rewrites it after two drafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template cannot tell whether a sentence matches this student's notes.

steps.what: Send the accepted brief to the other professionals
Meet those professionals and discuss students' needs
File the actions the professionals agreed

tasks.design: The {OTHER} record supplies the marks and the current support code into a {DOCS} brief. The class teacher accepts the brief, then sends that version from {EMAIL} to the professionals already on the {CALENDAR} invite. The meeting stays a conversation, and only the agreed action codes go back on the {OTHER} record.
tasks.previous_blocker: The brief mixes marks with support notes, and a wrong label can follow a child. Meetings are called per pupil, not as a batch.
tasks.enabler_now: The record already holds the marks and the support code, so the brief can be a query plus a traceable draft instead of a new judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Support notes can be health data. Other professionals disagree, and the talk cannot be replaced by the brief.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher and the other professionals decide the action together. The brief only starts the meeting.
tasks.altitude: The professional meeting still happens. The teacher still decides which brief is sent.

reach.task: Read the brief fields before a support meeting
reach.learn: the marks and support code the class teacher already accepted, so they are not retyped

evidence.claim: ParnasSys holds pupil records, marks and learning-goal tracking. The brief is a query of those stored fields, not a generated diagnosis, and it does not run the meeting.
Inferring pupils' emotions is banned, so the brief must not guess how a pupil feels.
Sharing the brief is pupil data. Parents and pupils have a say in pupil-data rules under the WMS, and WOR does not apply to schools.
An OPP is set within six weeks of enrolment after consulting parents and is evaluated yearly under WPO 40a. This meeting note is not an OPP.
The brief copies stored marks and does not evaluate learning outcomes, so it is not the high-risk use that evaluates learning outcomes.
Pupil data for this meeting is the school's public task. A support code can be health data. A new pupil-data system needs a data protection impact assessment.

assumptions: The focal boundary is the class teacher preparing the brief, attending the meeting and filing the actions. Other professionals' speaking time is not in this baseline.

Brief fields from {OTHER} are pupil id, subject, mark, mark date and the current support code. The support code may be special-category data the school already holds. The draft may not add a diagnosis or an emotion.
The recipient list is the professionals on the {CALENDAR} event. If the event has no list, the teacher types the addresses and the send stays manual.
This note is not an OPP. The 1.8 incremental hours are recipient-list fixes and briefs the trace check rejects, beyond the review step. Test native pupil-record fields before any custom screen.
unknowns: Which professionals are internal staff and which are external.
Whether support codes are health data in this school's record.
research_questions: How often is the professional meeting about one named pupil versus a general planning talk?

already_counted.description: The meeting with the other professionals stays with the class teacher.
The teacher still edits the brief, confirms recipients and types the action, owner and review date.

incremental.description: Fix recipient lists and rewrite briefs the trace check rejects, beyond the review already in the draft step.

approvals.approved_version: student brief version the class teacher accepted before sending

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The meeting stays. The saving is assembling the brief and not retyping it into the mail. The low end is a short case with no draft. The meeting hour is not claimed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set clear objectives for lessons, units and projects and tell the students.

steps.what: Read the goal codes for these units and projects
Establish clear objectives for the lessons

loop.input: The fixed goal-code list and this week's lesson topic.
loop.output: Objective lines, each with one goal code.
loop.check: Every objective maps to one code on that list and says what the student will do, and none assigns a pupil to a level.
loop.stop: The class teacher accepts this version or rewrites it after two drafts.
loop.why_not_simpler: A fixed objective bank cannot choose which goal code this week's lesson serves.

steps.what: Communicate those objectives to the students
File the accepted objectives on the lesson record

tasks.design: Goal codes already in the {LMS} are the only list a draft may use. The class teacher accepts the objective lines in {DOCS}, tells the students in the lesson, and the accepted version is filed on the {LMS} lesson record. The draft never scores a pupil or sets an education level.
tasks.previous_blocker: Objectives were rewritten from scratch even when the goal list was stable, and a generic bank did not say which code this lesson served.
tasks.enabler_now: A draft can propose lines that must map to an existing goal code, and the teacher accepts or rejects each line.
tasks.still_hard: Telling the class, and judging whether the objective fits this group, stays with the teacher. A missing goal code stops the draft.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher decides which code this lesson serves and says it in a way this class understands.

ambition.what: which goal code this lesson serves, including lessons that used to have no written objective.

tasks.altitude: Telling the students the objectives stays the teacher's hour. The teacher checks which goal code this lesson serves and still accepts the list.

reach.task: Keep the goal-code list current for elementary year groups
reach.learn: which codes the class teacher can map a lesson to

evidence.claim: Snappet drafts a class activity for the lesson goal. The teacher still accepts what is used. The source does not say the tool writes the objective list.
Snappet's piloted lesson suggestion proposes arithmetic lessons the teacher accepts or changes.

Oak's Aila, in a randomised trial of 464 primary teachers in 108 English schools, cut weekly preparation from 3.3 to 2.5 hours and quality was no worse. It covered 7% of lessons, use declined over ten weeks, and under one in five teachers felt it meaningfully influenced their teaching. That measures preparation time, not the minutes spent telling students the objective.
AI that evaluates learning outcomes or sets the education level is high-risk from 2 December 2027. This design does not score pupils or set their education level.

assumptions: The focal boundary is the class teacher setting objectives and telling the class. Communicating them is still the teacher's hour.

The {LMS} holds goal codes as code, short label and year group, maintained by the instructional coordinator. If a code is missing, the teacher does not invent one. The draft stops and the teacher writes the objectives in the old document. The draft saving does not apply in that case.

The filed record stores objective text, goal code and the accepted version id. The machine files only the version the teacher accepted. If the teacher changes the wording in the room, they edit that accepted version before it is filed.
Native lesson fields are tested before any custom screen. The 2 incremental hours per 100 baseline hours are remapping after the goal list changes, not the per-lesson edit already in the draft step.
unknowns: Whether the goal-code list is complete for elementary year groups.
What share of lessons already reuse last year's objectives.
research_questions: What share of lessons already start from a written objective?

already_counted.description: The teacher still edits the objective lines before accepting them.
Telling the students the objectives stays with the class teacher.

incremental.description: Remap objective lines after the goal list changes. The per-lesson edit is already in the draft step.

approvals.approved_version: objective list version the class teacher accepted

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Communicating objectives to students stays the whole of that step. The high end assumes the goal list is already coded and the teacher only edits the draft. The low end assumes most lessons reuse last year's objectives, in line with a primary trial that covered 7 percent of lessons and where use fell. The trial's preparation-time cut is not this task's saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The week is still lessons, parent meetings and talks with other professionals. Less time goes to hunting marks and rewriting objectives from a blank page. The class teacher still accepts every objective list, every pupil brief and every message to parents. Setting a pupil's education level, and sending a note the teacher has not read, stay outside this change.
reach: Special education teacher: use the filed priority and resource codes instead of asking the class teacher to retell the parent meeting.
Teaching assistant: show the stored lesson objective at the start of a small-group task.
Instructional coordinator: keep the goal-code list current so objective drafts map to codes the school still uses.
skills_to_grow: Check that each objective maps to a goal code before accepting it.
Write a pupil brief that cites a mark and avoids diagnostic labels.
role.ambitious_version: Every lesson opens from an accepted objective, and every parent or professional meeting starts from a mark extract the teacher has already corrected, so the hour is the conversation.

job.title: Elementary School Teachers, Except Special Education
